options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion

Sulphur is transformed from the organic form to the sulfate ion, the form of sulphur that higher plants absorb. Soil microorganisms oxidize not only organic sulphur but also sulphide minerals such as ferrous sulphide. The elemental sulphur is then oxidized to sulphate by sulphur bacteria.

821.subject: Chemistry
821.text: Bromine is added to cold dilute aqueous solution of $\mathrm{NaOH}$. The mixture is boiled. Which of the following statements is not true?
options: During the reaction bromine is present in four different oxidation states.
The greatest difference between the various oxidation states of bromine is 5 .
On acidification of the final mixture bromine is formed.
Disproportionation of bromine occurs during the reaction.
821.sol:
\begin{aligned}$& 2 \mathrm{NaOH}_{\text{(dilute) }}+\mathrm{Br}_{2} \\
& \stackrel{\text{ cold }}{\longrightarrow}  \mathrm{NaBrO}+\mathrm{NaBr}+\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}\\
& \underset{\text{ Sodium hypobromide }$}{3 $\mathrm{NaBrO}$} \stackrel{300 $\mathrm{ K}$}{\longrightarrow} 3 $\mathrm{NaBrO}
\end{aligned}On acidification, the $final mixture gives bromine.

\begin{aligned}$& 5 \mathrm{NaBrO}+\mathrm{NaBrO}_{3}+6  \mathrm{HCl} \longrightarrow\\
& 6 \mathrm{NaCl}+3  \mathrm{Br}_{2}$+3 $\mathrm{H}_{2}  \mathrm{O}
\end{aligned}Thus, during$ the $reaction, bromine is present in four different oxidation states i.e., zero in  \mathrm{Br}_2,+1 in  \mathrm{NaBrO}$,-1 in $\mathrm{NaBr}$ and $+5 in  \mathrm{NaBrO}_{3}. The greatest difference between various oxidation states of bromine is 6 and not 5. On acidification of the final mixture,  \mathrm{Br}_{2} is formed and disproportionation of  \mathrm{Br}_{2} occurs during the reaction giving  \mathrm{BrO}^{-}, \mathrm{Br}^{-} and  \mathrm{BrO}_{3}^{-}$ ions.

4909.subject: Chemistry
4909.text: Chlorine oxidises sulphur dioxide in the presence of water to give an oxyacid $A$. Chlorine also oxidises iodine in the presence of water to give an oxyacid $B$. The oxidation states of $\mathrm{S}$ and I in $A$ and $B$ are respectively
4909.sol:
(i) When chlorine oxidises sulphur dioxide in presence of water, it gives $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$ as oxyacid $(A)$. The reaction occurs as follows :
$\mathrm{Cl}_2+\mathrm{SO}_2+2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4+2 \mathrm{HCl}$
The oxidation number of sulphur in $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$ is
$2+x+(4 x-2)=0$
or, where $x=$ oxidation state of sulphur (S).
$x+2-8=0 \Rightarrow x=+6$
Hence, oxidation state of (S) in $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$ is (+) 6.
(ii) When chlorine $\left(\mathrm{Cl}_2\right)$ oxidises iodine $\left(\mathrm{I}_2\right)$ in presence of water, it gives $\mathrm{HIO}_3$ as oxyacid $(B)$, the reaction occurs as follows:
$5 \mathrm{Cl}_2+\mathrm{I}_2+6 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{HIO}_3+10 \mathrm{HCl} \text{. }$
The oxidation state of (I) in $\mathrm{HIO}_3$ is :
Let oxidation state of $(\mathrm{I})=x\begin{aligned}
& 1+x+3 \times(-2)=0 \\
& x+1-6=0 \Rightarrow x=+5
\end{aligned}$
Hence, oxidation state of iodine (I) in $\mathrm{HIO}_3$ is $=(+) 5$
Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.
4909.meta: Chlorine oxidises sulphur dioxide in the presence of water to give an oxyacid A . Chlorine also oxidises iodine in the presence of water to give an oxyacid B .

The point of contact of the circles

In circle $S_1$, centre $c_1=(-1,-1)$, radius $r_1=\sqrt{1+1-1}=1$ In circle $S_2$, centre $C_2=(1,-1)$, radius $r_2=\sqrt{1+1-1}=1$ Now, distance between two centre
$\begin{gathered}
C_1 C_2=\sqrt{(-1-1)^2+0} \\
=2
\end{gathered}$
Here, we see that
$C_1 C_2=r_1+r_2$
i.e., both circle touch externally.
So, point of contact of circle $S_1 and S_2=$ Mid-point of $C_1 and C_2=\left(\frac{-1+1}{2}, \frac{-1-1}{2}\right)=(0,-1)$

7493.subject: Mathematics
7493.text: If $z=1+i \sqrt{3}$ then $|\operatorname{Arg} z|+|\operatorname{Arg} \bar{z}|$ is equal to
7493.sol:
$z=1+i \sqrt{3}$
Let $1+i \sqrt{3}=r(\cos \theta+i \sin \theta)$
Then, $\quad r \cos \theta=1\ldots$ (i)
$r \sin \theta=\sqrt{3}\ldots$ (ii)
Eq. (i) + Eq. (ii), we get $r^2\left(\sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^2 \theta\right)=3+1\left(\because \sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^2 \theta=1\right)r^2=4r=2$
Eq. (ii) \div Eq. (i), we get
$\tan \theta=\sqrt{3}\Rightarrow \quad \tan \theta=\tan \frac{\pi}{3}\Rightarrow \quad \theta=\frac{\pi}{3}$
So, $z=(1+i \sqrt{3})=2\left\{\cos \frac{\pi}{3}+i \sin \frac{\pi}{3}\right\}$
Then $\bar{z}=(1-i \sqrt{3})=2\left\{\cos \frac{\pi}{3}-i \sin \frac{\pi}{3}\right\}=2\left\{\cos \left(\frac{-\pi}{3}\right)+i \sin \left(\frac{-\pi}{3}\right)\right\}$
So, $\quad \operatorname{Arg} z=\frac{\pi}{3}\operatorname{Arg} \bar{z}=-\frac{\pi}{3}|\operatorname{Arg} z|+|\operatorname{Arg} \bar{z}|=\left|\frac{\pi}{3}\right|+\left|\frac{-\pi}{3}\right|=\frac{\pi}{3}+\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{2 \pi}{3}$

So, required total ways of selecting at least one or more things from each category $=503-21-146=336$

For '$n$' observation ${x}_{1}, {x}_{2} \ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots.. {x}_{n}$, the mean deviation about their mean $\overset{¯}{x}$ is given by $M. D = \dfrac{{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}\left|{x}_{i} - \overset{¯}{x}\right|}{N}$. where $N$ is the number of observations

Now given data of numbers are $p, 6, 6, 7, 8, 11, 15$, and $16.$

So, mean $\overset{¯}{x} = \dfrac{p + 6 + 6 + 7 + 8 + 11 + 15 + 16}{8} = 3p$

$⇒ 23p = 69 ⇒ p = 3$

So given data is $3, 6, 6, 7, 8, 11, 15, 16$ and mean is $3p = 3 \times 3 = 9$.
$∴$ Mean deviation $= \dfrac{\left|3 - 9\right| + \left|6 - 9\right| + \left|6 - 9\right| + \left|7 - 9\right| + \left|8 - 9\right| + \left|11 - 9\right| + \left|15 - 9\right| + \left|16 - 9\right|}{8}$
Mean deviation $= \left|{x}_{i} - \overset{¯}{x}\right|n = \dfrac{30}{8} = 3. 75$

13815.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
13815.text: A particle of mass $' m '$, moving with a velocity $' v '$ makes an elastic collision in one dimension with a stationary particle of mass $' m '$. During the collision, they remain in contact with each other for an extremely small time $' T '$: Their force of contact, with time is shown in the figure. Then ${F}_{0} =$
13815.sol:
In an elastic head-on collision between two particles, the velocity of the particle gets exchanged, therefore net change of momentum of a particle is, $∆ p = m ∆ v = m\left(v - 0\right) = mv$

From newton's second law, the rate of change of momentum is force.

$F = \dfrac{d p}{d t} ⇒ F d t = d p ⇒ FT = ∆ p$

Here, $F$ is force of contact during the collision for a small-time $T$ that causes the $∆ p$change in momentum of particle.

Thus, the area under the graph of $F - t$curve gives the change in momentum.

$\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \left(\dfrac{T}{4}\right) \times \left({F}_{0}\right) + \left(\dfrac{3T}{4} - \dfrac{T}{4}\right) \times \left({F}_{0}\right) + \dfrac{1}{2} \times \left(T - \dfrac{3T}{4}\right) \times \left({F}_{0}\right) = \dfrac{3}{4}T{F}_{0}$

Therefore,

$\text{Area} = ∆ p ⇒ mv = \dfrac{3}{4}T{F}_{0} ⇒ {F}_{0} = \dfrac{4mv}{3T}$

20377.subject: Chemistry
20377.text: When 2-butyne is treated with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4/\text{HgSO}_4$, the product formed is:
20377.sol:
The reaction of an alkyne with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ in the presence of $\text{HgSO}_4$ is known as Kucherov's reaction, which results in the hydration of the alkyne.

For 2-butyne ($\text{CH}_3-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}_3$), the addition of a water molecule across the triple bond initially forms an unstable enol intermediate.

$\text{CH}_3-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{Hg}^{2+}, \text{H}^+} \text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{OH})=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3$

The enol intermediate undergoes tautomerization to form the more stable keto form, which is butanone.

$\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{OH})=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3 \rightleftharpoons \text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$

Thus, the final product is butanone.

Answer: Butanone

21324.subject: Mathematics
21324.text: The degree of the differential equation $\left[1+\left(\dfrac{d y}{d x}\right)^2\right]^{\dfrac{3}{4}}=\left(\dfrac{d^2 y}{d x^2}\right)^{\dfrac{1}{3}}$
21324.sol:
The given differential equation is $\left[1 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2\right]^{\dfrac{3}{4}} = \left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^{\dfrac{1}{3}}$.

To eliminate the fractional exponents, raise both sides to the power of $12$, which is the least common multiple of the denominators $4$ and $3$.

$\left(\left[1 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2\right]^{\dfrac{3}{4}}\right)^{12} = \left(\left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^{\dfrac{1}{3}}\right)^{12}$

Simplifying the exponents:

$\left[1 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2\right]^{9} = \left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^{4}$

The highest order derivative present in the equation is $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$, which is of order $2$.

The degree of a differential equation is the power of the highest order derivative when the equation is expressed as a polynomial in derivatives. Here, the power of $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ is $4$.

Therefore, the degree of the differential equation is $4$.

Answer: 4

21570.sol:
The integral is $I = \int e^x (1 + \tan x + \tan^2 x) dx$.

Using the identity $1 + \tan^2 x = \sec^2 x$, the expression becomes $I = \int e^x (\sec^2 x + \tan x) dx$.

Let $f(x) = \tan x$. Then $f'(x) = \sec^2 x$.

The integral is in the form $\int e^x (f(x) + f'(x)) dx$, which evaluates to $e^x f(x) + c$.

Therefore, $I = e^x \tan x + c$.

Answer: $e^x \tan x+c$

22012.sol:
The given sum is $S = \sum_{n=1}^{m} n \cdot n!$.

Observe that the general term can be written as $n \cdot n! = (n+1-1) \cdot n! = (n+1) \cdot n! - n!$.

Since $(n+1) \cdot n! = (n+1)!$, the term becomes $(n+1)! - n!$.

The summation is a telescoping series:

$S = \sum_{n=1}^{m} ((n+1)! - n!)$

$S = (2! - 1!) + (3! - 2!) + (4! - 3!) + \dots + ((m+1)! - m!)$

All intermediate terms cancel out, leaving only the last positive term and the first negative term:

$S = (m+1)! - 1!$

$S = (m+1)! - 1$.

Answer: $(m+1) !-1$

22588.subject: Physics
22588.text: Two identical conductors of lengths $l$ and 3$l$ respectively are maintained at the same temperature. They are given potential differences in the ratio $1: 3$. The ratio of their drift velocities is
22588.sol:
The drift velocity $v_d$ of electrons in a conductor is given by the formula $v_d = \dfrac{eE\tau}{m}$, where $E$ is the electric field, $e$ is the charge of an electron, $\tau$ is the relaxation time, and $m$ is the mass of the electron.

The electric field $E$ is related to the potential difference $V$ and length $l$ by $E = \dfrac{V}{l}$.

Substituting this into the drift velocity formula, we get $v_d = \dfrac{eV\tau}{ml}$.

For two conductors, the ratio of drift velocities is $\dfrac{v_{d1}}{v_{d2}} = \dfrac{V_1}{l_1} \times \dfrac{l_2}{V_2}$.

Given $l_1 = l$ and $l_2 = 3l$, and the ratio of potential differences $\dfrac{V_1}{V_2} = \dfrac{1}{3}$.

Substituting these values, we get $\dfrac{v_{d1}}{v_{d2}} = \dfrac{1}{l} \times \dfrac{3l}{3} = \dfrac{1}{1}$.

Answer: $1: 1$

22805.text: The electric field versus distance graph is shown as given. Select the correct statement from the following. E- electric field R-radius r - distance from the centre
options: The graph shows the variation of the electric field intensity with distance from the centre of a uniformly charged conducting ring of radius $R$.

The graph shows the variation of the electric field intensity with distance from the centre of a uniformly charged conducting solid sphere of radius $R$.
22805.sol:
The electric field $E$ inside a uniformly charged non-conducting solid sphere of radius $R$ at a distance $r$ from the center is given by $E = \dfrac{kQr}{R^3}$, which implies $E \propto r$. This corresponds to the linear increase in the graph for $r < R$.

Outside the sphere, for $r > R$, the electric field is given by $E = \dfrac{kQ}{r^2}$, which implies $E \propto \dfrac{1}{r^2}$. This corresponds to the curve decreasing as $r$ increases for $r > R$.

The graph shows a linear increase up to $r = R$ and a non-linear decrease for $r > R$, which is the characteristic behavior of the electric field of a uniformly charged non-conducting solid sphere.

Answer: The graph shows the variation of the electric field intensity with distance from the centre of a uniformly charged non conducting solid sphere of radius $R$.

23345.text: A biconvex lens has two different refractive indices in different regions. The upper half has a refractive index 1.7 and the lower half has a refractive index 1.5. The radius of curvatures of the two surfaces are $R_1=15 \mathrm{ cm}$ and $R_2=-25 \mathrm{ cm}$. Image of a distant object will be formed at:
23345.sol:
The focal length $f$ of a lens is given by the lens maker formula: $\dfrac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1) \left( \dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2} \right).

For the upper half, the refractive index $\mu_1 = 1.7$. Given $R_1 = 15 $\text{ cm} and $ R_2 = -25 $\text{ cm}, the focal length $ f_1$ is calculated as:

\dfrac{1}{f_1} = (1.7 - 1) \left( \dfrac{1}{15} - \dfrac{1}{-25} \right) =0.7 \left( \dfrac{1}{15} + \dfrac{1}{25} \right) =0.7 \left( \dfrac{5 + 3}{75} \right) =0.7 \times \dfrac{8}{75} = \dfrac{5.6}{75}.

$ f_1 = $\dfrac{75}{5.6} \approx13.39 \text{ cm}.

For the lower half, the refractive index $\mu_2 = 1.5$. The focal length $f_2$ is calculated as:

\dfrac{1}{f_2} = (1.5 - 1) \left( \dfrac{1}{15} - \dfrac{1}{-25} \right) =0.5 \left( \dfrac{1}{15} + \dfrac{1}{25} \right) =0.5 \left( \dfrac{8}{75} \right) = \dfrac{4}{75}.

$ f_2 = $\dfrac{75}{4} =18.75 \text{ cm}.

Since the object is at infinity, the images are formed at the focal points of the respective halves, which are 13.39 \text{ cm} and 18.75 \text{ cm}.$

Answer: 13.39 cm and 18.75 cm

23426.text: A bullet, fired into a door gets embedded exactly at it's centre, causing the door to rotate about it's vertical axis, practically without friction, with an angular velocity of $0.625\ rads^{-1}$. The door is 1.0 m wide and weighs 12 kg. If the mass of the bullet is 10g, find the speed with which it was fired. (Hint: The moment of inertia of the door about the vertical axis at one end is $\dfrac{ML^2}{3}$).
23426.sol:
By conservation of angular momentum about the vertical axis of the door:

$L_i = L_f$

$m v r = (I_{door} + I_{bullet}) \omega$

$m v \left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{ML^2}{3} + m\left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right)^2\right) \omega$

Substituting the given values $M = 12\ kg$, $L = 1.0\ m$, $m = 0.01\ kg$, and $\omega = 0.625\ rads^{-1}$:

$0.01 \times v \times 0.5 = \left(\dfrac{12 \times 1^2}{3} + 0.01 \times 0.5^2\right) \times 0.625$

$0.005 v = (4 + 0.0025) \times 0.625$

Neglecting the small term $0.0025$ compared to $4$:

$0.005 v = 4 \times 0.625$

$0.005 v = 2.5$

$v = \dfrac{2.5}{0.005} = 500\ ms^{-1}$

27420.subject: Chemistry
27420.text: Both human DNA and RNA are chiral molecules. The chirality in DNA and RNA arises due to the presence of
27420.sol: DNA and RNA are chiral molecules due to their structural components. Both contain pentose sugars: DNA contains deoxyribose and RNA contains ribose. These are D-sugars with multiple chiral centers (at $C_2$, $C_3$, and $C_4$ in the furanose ring). The D-designation comes from the stereochemical configuration at the chiral center furthest from the carbonyl carbon. The chiral centers in these sugar moieties are the primary source of chirality in nucleic acids, making them optically active molecules. While the phosphate units and bases also contribute to molecular structure, the fundamental chirality arises from the D-sugar component.

29361.text:
The specific conductance of $0 . 0025M$ acetic acid is $5 \times {10}^{- 5}S{cm}^{- 1}$ at a certain temperature. The dissociation constant of acetic acid is ___________ $\times {10}^{- 7}$.(Nearest integer)

Consider limiting molar conductivity of ${CH}_{3}COOH$ as $400S{cm}^{2}{mol}^{- 1}$
29361.sol:
The relation between Molar conductance ${\lambda}_{m}$ and specific conductance $κ$ is

${\lambda}_{m} = \dfrac{k \times 1000}{M}$

M = molarity

${\lambda}_{m} = \dfrac{\left(5 \times {10}^{- 5}\right) \times \left({10}^{3}\right)}{\left(2 . 5 \times {10}^{- 3}\right)} = 20S{cm}^{2}{mol}^{- 1}$

Now, the degree of dissociation, $\alpha = \dfrac{{\lambda}_{m}}{{\lambda}^{\infty}}$

$\alpha = \dfrac{20}{400} = \dfrac{1}{20}$

The acid dissociation constant, ${K}_{a} = \dfrac{{C \alpha}^{2}}{( 1 - \alpha )} = \dfrac{\left(2 . 5 \times {10}^{- 3}\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{20} \times \dfrac{1}{20}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{19}{20}\right)}$

$= 65 . 789 \times {10}^{– 7}$

$\approx 66 \times {10}^{– 7}$

29794.text:
The ascending order of acidity of $– OH$ group in the following compounds is :

      (A) $Bu – OH$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
29794.sol:
The decrease in electron density of the $O - H$ bond of o,p-dinitrophenol, the polarity of $O - H$ bond decreases. The electron withdrawing group $\left(- {NO}_{2}\right)$), withdraws electrons and disperses the negative charge. Therefore, $- {NO}_{2}$ group stabilizes the phenoxide ion. Hence, o,p-dinitrophenol is more acidic than p-nitrophenol and phenol.

$OMe$ is an electron donating group, hence it increases electron density, there why making it less acidic.

$Bu - OH$ is an aliphatic alcohol. In phenoxide ion the negative charge is delocalized within the ring structure which makes it more stable than the aliphatic alcohols. In aliphatic alcohols there is no such delocalization stabilization. Therefore, phenols are more acidic and the resulting phenoxide ion is stabilized because of resonance.

35714.text:
If $\alpha > \beta > 0$ are the roots of the equation $a{x}^{2} + bx + 1 = 0$, and
$\lim_{x \to \dfrac{1}{\alpha}}\left(\dfrac{1 - cos\left({x}^{2} + bx + a\right)}{2 ( 1 - \alphax{)}^{2}}\right)\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{k}\left(\dfrac{1}{\beta} - \dfrac{1}{\alpha}\right)$, then $k$ is equal to
35714.sol:
Since, $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of the equation $a{x}^{2} + bx + 1 = 0$, therefore $\dfrac{1}{\alpha}$ and $\dfrac{1}{\beta}$ would be the roots of ${x}^{2} + bx + a = 0$.

Let

$L = \lim_{x \to \dfrac{1}{\alpha}}\left[\dfrac{1 - cos\left({x}^{2} + bx + a\right)}{2{\left(1 - \alphax\right)}^{2}}\right]\dfrac{1}{2} \to \dfrac{0}{0}$

$⇒ L = \lim_{x \to \dfrac{1}{\alpha}}\left[\dfrac{2\sin^{2}\left(\dfrac{{x}^{2} + bx + a}{2}\right)}{2{\left(1 - \alphax\right)}^{2}}\right]\dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ L = \lim_{x \to \dfrac{1}{\alpha}}\left[\dfrac{\sin^{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\left(x - \dfrac{1}{\alpha}\right)\left(x - \dfrac{1}{\beta}\right)\right)}{{\alpha}^{2}{\left(x - \dfrac{1}{\alpha}\right)}^{2}}\right]\dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ L = \lim_{x \to \dfrac{1}{\alpha}}\left[\dfrac{{\left(x - \dfrac{1}{\beta}\right)}^{2}}{4{\alpha}^{2}} \times \dfrac{{\left\{sin\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\left(x - \dfrac{1}{\alpha}\right)\left(x - \dfrac{1}{\beta}\right)\right)\right\}}^{2}}{{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{2}{\left(x - \dfrac{1}{\alpha}\right)}^{2}{\left(x - \dfrac{1}{\beta}\right)}^{2}}\right]\dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ L = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{1}{\alpha} - \dfrac{1}{\beta}\right)}{2\alpha}$

On comparing this value with the value given in the question we get, $k = 2\alpha$.

Hence this is the correct option.

37267.text: Let $a, b$ and $c$ be in $G . P .$ with common ratio $r,$ where $a \ne 0$ and $0 < r \le \dfrac{1}{2} .$ If $3a, 7b$ and $15c$ are the first three terms of an $A . P . ,$ then the ${4}^{th}$ term of this $A . P .$ is :
37267.sol:
We know that, the ${n}^{th}$ term of a $G . P .$ with first term $a$ and common ratio $r$ is ${t}_{n} = a{r}^{n - 1} .$

Then, $b = ar$ and $c = a{r}^{2}$

Now, $3a, 7b$ and $15c$ are in $A . P .$

$⇒ 14b = 3a + 15c$

$⇒ 14\left(ar\right) = 3a + 15 ( a{r}^{2} )$

$⇒ 14r = 3 + 15{r}^{2}$

$⇒ 15{r}^{2} - 14r + 3 = 0$

$⇒ \left(3r - 1\right)\left(5r - 3\right) = 0$

$⇒ r = \dfrac{1}{3}$ or $r = \dfrac{3}{5}$

The only acceptable value is $r = \dfrac{1}{3},$ because $r \in \left(0, \dfrac{1}{2}\right]$

$∴$ the first term of the $A . P .$ is $A = 3a$ and the common difference is $d = 7b - 3a = 7ar - 3a = \dfrac{7}{3}a - 3a = - \dfrac{2}{3}a$

Also, we know that the ${n}^{th}$ term of an $A . P .$ with first term $A$ and common difference $d$ is ${T}_{n} = A + \left(n - 1\right)d$

$∴ {T}_{4} = 3a + \left(4 - 1\right)\left(- \dfrac{2}{3}a\right) = 3a - 2a = a .$

37801.sol:
Let, coordinate of centroid is $( h, k )$ and coordinate of point $P$ is $( \alpha, \beta )$

We know that the centroid of a triangle with vertices $\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right), \left({x}_{2}, {y}_{2}\right) and \left({x}_{3}, {y}_{3}\right) is \left(\dfrac{{x}_{1} + {x}_{2} + {x}_{3}}{3}, \dfrac{{y}_{1} + {y}_{2} + {y}_{3}}{3}\right) .

Hence,$ in ∆ PQR,$ we have \dfrac{\alpha + 1 + 3}{3} =$h and $\dfrac{\beta + 4 - 2}{3} =k$

Hence, $2\left(3h - 4\right) - 3\left(3k - 2\right) + 4 = 0$

$⇒ 6h - 9k + 2 = 0$

For finding the locus replace $\left(h, k\right)$ by $\left(x, y\right)$

Hence, the locus of centroid is $6x - 9y + 2 = 0$ which has slope $= - \dfrac{6}{\left(- 9\right)$} = $\dfrac{2}{3} since$ the slope of a lineax + by + c = 0$ is $- $\dfrac{a}{b} .

39101.subject: Physics
39101.text: The space between the plates of a parallel plate capacitor of capacitance C (without any dielectric) is now filled with three dielectric slabs of dielectric constants $K_{1}=2, K_{2}=3$ and $K_{3}=5$ (as shown in figure). If new capacitance is $\frac{n}{3} C$ then the value of $n$ is $\_\_\_\_$.
39101.sol:
The initial capacitance is $C = \frac{\epsilon_0 A}{d}$.
From the figure, the capacitor is divided into three parts.
The bottom half is divided into two capacitors $C_2$ and $C_3$ in parallel, each with area $A/2$ and thickness $d/2$.
$C_2 = \frac{K_2 \epsilon_0 (A/2)}{d/2} = K_2 \frac{\epsilon_0 A}{d} = 3C$
$C_3 = \frac{K_3 \epsilon_0 (A/2)}{d/2} = K_3 \frac{\epsilon_0 A}{d} = 5C$
The equivalent capacitance of the bottom part is $C_{eq, bottom} = C_2 + C_3 = 3C + 5C = 8C$.
The top half is a single capacitor $C_1$ with area $A$ and thickness $d/2$.
$C_1 = \frac{K_1 \epsilon_0 A}{d/2} = 2K_1 \frac{\epsilon_0 A}{d} = 2(2)C = 4C$.
The total capacitance $C'$ is the series combination of $C_1$ and $C_{eq, bottom}$.
$\frac{1}{C'} = \frac{1}{C_1} + \frac{1}{C_{eq, bottom}} = \frac{1}{4C} + \frac{1}{8C} = \frac{2+1}{8C} = \frac{3}{8C}$
$C' = \frac{8}{3}C$
Comparing with $C' = \frac{n}{3}C$, we get $n = 8$.

$= \dfrac{6}{5} \times 5\mu F = 6\mu F$.

40539.text: A dipole comprises of two charged particles of identical magnitude $q$ and opposite in nature. The mass $m$ of the positive charged particle is half of the mass of the negative charged particle. The two charges are separated by a distance $l$ . If the dipole is placed in a uniform electric field $\overset{\to}{E}$; in such a way that dipole axis makes a very small angle with the electric field, $\overset{\to}{E}$. The angular frequency of the oscillations of the dipole when released is given by:
40539.sol:
The data given is

$l =$distance between the charges

$q =$charge

$m =$mass of the positive charge

$2m$$=$mass of negative charge

The moment of inertia of the system is

$I = \left(\dfrac{m \times 2m}{m + 2m}\right){\left(l\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{2m{l}^{2}}{3}$

The angular frequency can be written as

$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{pE}{I}} . . . ( i )$

Substituting the value of moment of inertia in the equation (i) we get

$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{pE}{\dfrac{2m{l}^{2}}{3}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3pE}{2m{l}^{2}}}$

The value of the dipole moment is

$p = ql$

Hence, the angular frequency becomes

$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{3qE}{2ml}}$

Given that $\dfrac{{m}_{1}}{{m}_{2}} = \dfrac{4}{3}, \dfrac{{r}_{1}}{{r}_{2}} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

Now the total energy of a satellite $TE = \dfrac{1}{2}m{{v}_{o}}^{2} + \left(\dfrac{- GMm}{r}\right)$

Since the orbital speed of a satellite ${v}_{o} = \sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{r}}$

$⇒ TE = - \dfrac{GMm}{2r} ∝ \dfrac{m}{r}$

$⇒ \dfrac{T{E}_{1}}{T{E}_{2}} = \dfrac{{m}_{1}}{{m}_{2}} \cdot \dfrac{{r}_{2}}{{r}_{1}} = \dfrac{4}{3} \times \dfrac{4}{3} = \dfrac{16}{9}$

42853.subject: Physics
42853.text: A ray of light passing through an equilateral prism is having velocity $2.12 \times 10^8$ m/s in the prism material, then the minimum angle of deviation is _________ degrees.
42853.sol:
Velocity of light in vacuum, $c = 3 \times 10^8$ m/s

Velocity of light in the prism, $v = 2.12 \times 10^8$ m/s

Refractive index of the prism material, $\mu = \dfrac{c}{v} = \dfrac{3 \times 10^8}{2.12 \times 10^8} \approx 1.414 \approx \sqrt{2}$

For an equilateral prism, the angle of the prism $A = 60^\circ$.

Using the prism formula:

$\mu = \dfrac{\sin\left(\dfrac{A + \delta_m}{2}\right)}{\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)}$

$\sqrt{2} = \dfrac{\sin\left(\dfrac{60^\circ + \delta_m}{2}\right)}{\sin(30^\circ)}$

$\sqrt{2} = \dfrac{\sin\left(30^\circ + \dfrac{\delta_m}{2}\right)}{\dfrac{1}{2}}$

$\sin\left(30^\circ + \dfrac{\delta_m}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$30^\circ + \dfrac{\delta_m}{2} = 45^\circ$

$\dfrac{\delta_m}{2} = 15^\circ$

$\delta_m = 30^\circ$

Answer: $30$

42986.text: A microscope was initially placed in air (refractive index $1$). It is then immersed in oil (refractive index $2$). For a light whose wavelength in air is $\lambda$, calculate the change of microscope's resolving power due to oil and choose the correct option
options: Resolving power will be $\dfrac{1}{4}$ in the oil than it was in the air
Resolving power will be twice in the oil than it was in the air.
Resolving power will be four times in the oil than it was in the air.
Resolving power will be $\dfrac{1}{2}$ in the oil than it was in the air.
42986.sol:
Resolving power of microscope in air is $( R . P{)}_{air} = \dfrac{2{\mu}_{air}sin\theta}{1 . 22\lambda} = \dfrac{2sin\theta}{1 . 22\lambda}$

$( R . P{)}_{oil} = \dfrac{2{\mu}_{oil}sin\theta}{1 . 22{\lambda}_{oil}} = \dfrac{2sin\theta\left(2\right)}{1 . 22\lambda}$

${\left(R . P\right)}_{oil} = {\left(R . P\right)}_{air} \times 2$

Thus, resolving power in oil is twice the resolving power in air.

43431.subject: Physics
43431.text: If $X$ and $Y$ are the inputs, the given circuit works as _______.
43431.sol:
The circuit consists of four NAND gates.

The first two NAND gates have their inputs tied together, acting as NOT gates. Their outputs are $\overline{X}$ and $\overline{Y}$.

These outputs are fed into the third NAND gate. The output of this gate is:
$y' = \overline{\overline{X} \cdot \overline{Y}}$

Using De Morgan's theorem:
$y' = \overline{\overline{X}} + \overline{\overline{Y}} = X + Y$

This output is fed into the fourth NAND gate, which also has its inputs tied together, acting as a NOT gate. The final output is:
Output $= \overline{X + Y}$

This represents the Boolean expression for a NOR gate.

Answer: NOR gate

44376.subject: Physics
44376.text: The equation of a plane progressive wave is given by $y = 5\cos\pi\left(200t - \dfrac{x}{150}\right)$ where $x$ and $y$ are in cm and $t$ is in second. The velocity of the wave is _______ m/s.
44376.sol:
The given equation of the wave is $y = 5\cos\pi\left(200t - \dfrac{x}{150}\right)$

Rewriting the equation, we get $y = 5\cos\left(200\pi t - \dfrac{\pi x}{150}\right)$

Comparing this with the standard wave equation $y = A\cos(\omega t - kx)$, we have:

$\omega = 200\pi$ rad/s

$k = \dfrac{\pi}{150}$ rad/cm

The velocity of the wave is given by $v = \dfrac{\omega}{k}$

$v = \dfrac{200\pi}{\dfrac{\pi}{150}} = 30000$ cm/s

Converting to m/s, we get $v = \dfrac{30000}{100} = 300$ m/s

Answer: $300$

45889.subject: Chemistry
45889.text: Which one of the following electrolytes has the same value of van't Hoff factor (i) as that of $\mathrm{K}_4\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]$ ?
45889.sol:
The value of van't Hoff factor of the given molecule is as follows :
$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{Al}_2\left(\mathrm{SO}_4\right)_3 & \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{Al}^{3+}+3 \mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}, \mathrm{i}=5 \\ \mathrm{~K}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4 & \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{~K}^{+}+\mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}, \mathrm{i}=3 \\ \mathrm{~K}_3\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right] & \rightleftharpoons 3 \mathrm{~K}^{+}+\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{3+}, \mathrm{i}=4 \\ \mathrm{Al}\left(\mathrm{NO}_3\right)_3 & \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{Al}^{3+}+3 \mathrm{NO}_3^{-}, \mathrm{i}=4\end{aligned}$
The van't Hoff factor for $\mathrm{K}_4\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]$ is
$\mathrm{K}_4\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right] \rightleftharpoons 4 \mathrm{~K}^{+}+\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{4-}, \mathrm{i}=5$
$\therefore \mathrm{Al}_2\left(\mathrm{SO}_4\right)_3$ has the same value of van't Hoff factor as that of $\mathrm{K}_4\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]$.

46640.text: The temperature of the black body increases from $T$ to $2 T$. The factor by which the rate of emission will increase, is?

Hence,
$\frac{E_1}{E_2}=\frac{T_1^4}{T_2^4}=\left(\frac{T}{2 T}\right)^4=\frac{1}{16}$
$\therefore \quad E_2=16 E_1$

53969.text: Suppose $a, b, c$ are in AP and $a^2, b^2, c^2$ are in GP. If $a < b < c$ and $a+b+c=\frac{3}{2}$, then the value of $a$ is
53969.sol:
Since, $a, b, c$ are in AP.
$\therefore \quad a=A-D, b=A, c=A+D$
Where, $A$ is the first term and $D$ is the common difference of an AP.
Given,
$a+b+c=\frac{3}{2}$
$\begin{array}{rrr}
\Rightarrow & (A-D)+A+(A+D) & =\frac{3}{2} \\
\Rightarrow & 3 A & =\frac{3}{2} \\
\Rightarrow & A & =\frac{1}{2}
\end{array}$
$\therefore$ The numbers are $\frac{1}{2}-D, \frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{2}+D$
Also, $\left(\frac{1}{2}-D\right)^2, \frac{1}{4},\left(\frac{1}{2}+D\right)^2$ are in GP.
$\Rightarrow \quad\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^2=\left(\frac{1}{2}-D\right)^2\left(\frac{1}{2}+D\right)^2$
$\begin{array}{ll}
\Rightarrow & \frac{1}{16}=\left(\frac{1}{4}-D^2\right)^2 \\
\Rightarrow & \frac{1}{4}-D^2= \pm \frac{1}{4} \\
\Rightarrow & \quad D^2=\left(\frac{1}{2} D=0 \text{ is not possible }\right) \\
\Rightarrow & D= \pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\
\therefore & a=\frac{1}{2} \pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}
\end{array}$
So, out of the given value $a=\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ is the right choice.

54071.subject: Mathematics
54071.text: The maximum value of $\left(\cos \alpha_1\right) \cdot\left(\cos \alpha_2\right) \ldots\left(\cos \alpha_n\right) . \quad$ Under the restrictions $0 \leq \alpha_1, \alpha_2, \ldots \alpha_n \leq \frac{\pi}{2} \quad and \left(\cot \alpha_1\right) \cdot\left(\cot \alpha_2\right) \ldots\left(\cot \alpha_n\right)=1$ is
54071.sol:
We are given that,
$\left(\cot \alpha_1\right) \cdot\left(\cot \alpha_2\right) \ldots\left(\cot \alpha_n\right)=1$
$\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow\left(\cos \alpha_1 \cdot\left(\cos \alpha_2\right) \ldots\left(\cos \alpha_n\right)=\left(\sin \alpha_1\right)\right. \\ \cdot\left(\sin \alpha_2\right) \ldots\left(\sin \alpha_n\right)\end{aligned}$  ....(i)
Let $y=\left(\cos \alpha_1\right) \cdot\left(\cos \alpha_2\right) \ldots\left(\cos \alpha_n\right) \quad$ (to be max.) Squarring both sides, we get
$y^2=\left(\cos ^2 \alpha_1\right) \cdot\left(\cos ^2 \alpha_2\right) \ldots\left(\cos ^2 \alpha_n\right)$
$=\cos \alpha_1 \cdot \sin \alpha_1 \cdot \cos \alpha_2 \cdot \sin \alpha_2 \ldots \cos \alpha_n \cdot \sin \alpha_n$ [using (i)]
$=\frac{1}{2^n}\left[\sin 2 \alpha_1 \cdot \sin 2 \alpha_2 \ldots \sin 2 \alpha_n\right]$
As $\quad 0 \leq \alpha_1, \alpha_2, \ldots, \alpha_n \leq \frac{\pi}{2}$
$\therefore \quad 0 \leq 2 \alpha_1, 2 \alpha_2, \ldots, 2 \alpha_n \leq \pi$
$\Rightarrow 0 \leq \sin 2 \alpha_1, \sin 2 \alpha_2, \ldots, \sin 2 \alpha_n \leq 1$
$\therefore y^2 \leq \frac{1}{2^n} \cdot 1 \quad \Rightarrow y \leq \frac{1}{2^{n / 2}}$
$\therefore$ Maximum value of $y$ is $\frac{1}{2^{n / 2}}$.

54853.subject: Chemistry
54853.text: Which of the following reagents limits the oxidation of $\text{R-CH}_2\text{OH}$ up to R-CHO only?
54853.sol:
Primary alcohols ($\text{R-CH}_2\text{OH}$) can be oxidized to aldehydes ($\text{R-CHO}$) or carboxylic acids ($\text{R-COOH}$) depending on the oxidizing agent used.

Strong oxidizing agents like acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$, $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ / dil. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, and $\text{CrO}_3$ in aqueous medium oxidize primary alcohols directly to carboxylic acids.

To limit the oxidation to the aldehyde stage, mild oxidizing agents are required. Pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) is a mild oxidizing agent that selectively oxidizes primary alcohols to aldehydes and prevents further oxidation to carboxylic acids.

$\text{R-CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{PCC}} \text{R-CHO}$

Answer: PCC

55116.subject: Chemistry
55116.text:
Identify the product 'B' in the following reaction
$\text{Isopropyl cyanide} \xrightarrow{\large{\text{SnCl}_2, \text{HCl}}} \text{A} \xrightarrow{\large{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+}} \text{B} + \text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$
55116.sol:
The given reaction is Stephen reduction.

Isopropyl cyanide is $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CN}$.

When isopropyl cyanide is treated with $\text{SnCl}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$, it undergoes reduction to form an imine hydrochloride intermediate (A).

$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CN} + 2[\text{H}] + \text{HCl} \xrightarrow{\text{SnCl}_2, \text{HCl}} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}=\text{NH}\cdot\text{HCl}$ (A)

Acidic hydrolysis of the imine hydrochloride yields the corresponding aldehyde (B).

$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}=\text{NH}\cdot\text{HCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CHO} + \text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$

The product B is $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CHO}$, which is 2-methylpropanal.

Answer: 2-Methylpropanal

What is order and molecularity of following reaction?
$\mathrm{NO}_{2(\mathrm{ g})}+\mathrm{NO}_{2(\mathrm{ g})} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{NO}_{(\mathrm{g})}+\mathrm{O}_{2(\mathrm{ g})}$
56053.sol:
Molecularity refers to the number of reacting species involved in an elementary step. In this reaction, two $\mathrm{NO}_2$ molecules collide, so the molecularity is 2.

For elementary reactions, the order equals molecularity with rate law determined directly from stoichiometry. The reaction $2\mathrm{NO}_{2(\mathrm{g})} \to 2\mathrm{NO}_{(\mathrm{g})} + \mathrm{O}_{2(\mathrm{g})}$ implies $\text{Rate} = k[\mathrm{NO}_2]^2$, making the order 2.

Since both order and molecularity are 2, the correct choice is $\boxed{\text{B}}$.

57770.subject: Chemistry
57770.text: $200$ mL of ethylene gas and $150$ mL of HCl gas were allowed to react at $1$ bar. Pressure to form gaseous ethyl chloride. What is the work done during the reaction?
57770.sol:
The balanced chemical equation for the reaction is:

$C_2H_4(g) + HCl(g) \rightarrow C_2H_5Cl(g)$

Initial volumes:
$V_{C_2H_4} = 200$ mL
$V_{HCl} = 150$ mL

Total initial volume $V_i = 200 + 150 = 350$ mL.

Since the reaction occurs at constant pressure and temperature, the volumes of gases are directly proportional to their number of moles. Here, $HCl$ is the limiting reagent.

Volume of $C_2H_4$ reacted = $150$ mL
Volume of $C_2H_4$ remaining = $200 - 150 = 50$ mL
Volume of $C_2H_5Cl$ formed = $150$ mL

Total final volume $V_f = 50 + 150 = 200$ mL.

Change in volume $\Delta V = V_f - V_i = 200 - 350 = -150$ mL = $-0.15$ L.

The work done during the reaction at constant pressure is given by:

$W = -P \Delta V$

Substituting the values:

$W = -1 \text{ bar} \times (-0.15 \text{ L}) = 0.15 \text{ L bar}$

Since $1 \text{ L bar} = 100 \text{ J}$, we get:

$W = 0.15 \times 100 \text{ J} = 15 \text{ J}$

Answer: $15$ J

57959.subject: Chemistry
57959.text: What is the pH of solution containing $5 \times 10^{-4}\ \text{M}\ \text{H}^+$ ion?
57959.sol:
The pH of a solution is given by the negative logarithm of the hydrogen ion concentration:

$\text{pH} = -\log[\text{H}^+]$

Given $[\text{H}^+] = 5 \times 10^{-4}\ \text{M}$

$\text{pH} = -\log(5 \times 10^{-4})$

$\text{pH} = -(\log 5 + \log 10^{-4})$

$\text{pH} = -(\log 5 - 4)$

$\text{pH} = 4 - \log 5$

Using the value $\log 5 \approx 0.699$:

$\text{pH} = 4 - 0.699 = 3.301$

Answer: $3.301$

60256.subject: Mathematics
60256.text: The combined equation of the tangent and normal to the curve $x y=100$ at the point $(5,20)$ is ________.
60256.sol:
Combined equation of tangent and normal to the curve $xy=100$ at point $(5,20)$

The curve $xy=100$ has derivative $\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{y}{x}$ by implicit differentiation. At point $(5,20)$, the tangent slope is $m_t = -\frac{20}{5} = -4$.

The tangent equation using point-slope form: $y - 20 = -4(x - 5)$ simplifies to $4x + y - 40 = 0$.

The normal slope is the negative reciprocal: $m_n = \frac{1}{4}$, giving the normal equation $y - 20 = \frac{1}{4}(x - 5)$ which simplifies to $x - 4y + 75 = 0$.

The combined equation of tangent and normal is the product of their equations:

$(4x + y - 40)(x - 4y + 75) = 0$

Expanding yields:

$4x^2 - 15xy - 4y^2 + 260x + 235y - 3000 = 0$

This equation does not match options A, B, or C, confirming the answer is $\boxed{D}$.

60352.text: The equation of the normal to the curve $x=\theta+\sin \theta, y=1+\cos \theta$ at $\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}$ is
60352.sol:

& x=\theta+\sin \theta, y=1+\cos \theta \\
& \frac{\mathrm{d} x}{\mathrm{ d} \theta}=1+\cos \theta, \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{ d} \theta}=-\sin \theta \\
& \therefore \quad \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{ d} x}=\frac{\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{ d} \theta}}{\frac{\mathrm{ d} x}{\mathrm{ d} \theta}}=\frac{-\sin \theta}{1+\cos \theta} \\
& \left.\therefore \quad \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{dx}}\right|_{\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}}=\frac{-\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)}{1+\cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)}=\frac{-1}{1+0}=-1
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& \text{ At } \theta=\frac{\pi}{2} \\
& x=\frac{\pi}{2}+\sin \frac{\pi}{2}=1+\frac{\pi}{2}, y=1+\cos \frac{\pi}{2}=1
\end{aligned}\therefore \quad$ Equation of the normal is
$\begin{array}{ll} & (y-1)=\frac{-1}{\left(\left.\frac{\mathrm{ d} y}{\mathrm{ d} x}\right|_{\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}}\right)}\left(x-1-\frac{\pi}{2}\right) \\
\therefore \quad & (y-1)=1\left(x-1-\frac{\pi}{2}\right) \\

\end{array}$

60836.text: Let z be the complex number such that $|\mathrm{z}|+\mathrm{z}=3+\mathrm{i}$ where $i=\sqrt{-1}$, then $|\mathrm{z}|=$
60836.sol:
Let $z = x + iy$ where $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$ with modulus $|z| = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}$. Given the equation $|z| + z = 3 + i$, substitute to obtain:

$\sqrt{x^2 + y^2} + x + iy = 3 + i$

Equating real and imaginary parts yields $y = 1$ and $\sqrt{x^2 + 1} + x = 3$.

Solving the real equation: $\sqrt{x^2 + 1} = 3 - x$. Squaring both sides gives $x^2 + 1 = 9 - 6x + x^2$, which simplifies to $6x = 8$, so $x = \frac{4}{3}$.

Thus $z = \frac{4}{3} + i$ and $|z| = \sqrt{(\frac{4}{3})^2 + 1^2} = \sqrt{\frac{16}{9} + \frac{9}{9}} = \sqrt{\frac{25}{9}} = \frac{5}{3}$.

61333.text: $The order and degree of the differential equation \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{d} x}}-4 \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{d} x}-7 x=0$ is respectively
61333.sol:
The order of the differential equation is determined by the highest derivative present, which is the first derivative $\frac{dy}{dx}$ in this case.

To determine the degree, the equation must first be rationalized. We isolate the radical: $\sqrt{\frac{dy}{dx}} = 4\frac{dy}{dx} + 7x$, and square both sides, yielding $\frac{dy}{dx} = \left(4\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 + 2\left(4\frac{dy}{dx}\right)(7x) + (7x)^2 = 16\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 + 56x\frac{dy}{dx} + 49x^2$.

The highest power of $\frac{dy}{dx}$ in the resulting expression is 2, so the degree is 2. The order is 1 and the degree is 2.

The correct option is A.

62023.subject: Mathematics
62023.text: The function defined by $\mathrm{f}(x)=\frac{2 x+3}{3 x+4}, x \neq-\frac{4}{3}$ is
62023.sol:
To test the injectivity of $f(x) = rac{2x + 3}{3x + 4}$, where $x eq - rac{4}{3}$, suppose $f(x_1) = f(x_2)$. This implies $ rac{2x_1 + 3}{3x_1 + 4} = rac{2x_2 + 3}{3x_2 + 4}$.

Cross-multiplying gives $(2x_1 + 3)(3x_2 + 4) = (2x_2 + 3)(3x_1 + 4)$.

Expanding both sides yields $6x_1x_2 + 8x_1 + 9x_2 + 12 = 6x_1x_2 + 8x_2 + 9x_1 + 12$.

Subtracting $6x_1x_2 + 12$ from both sides gives $8x_1 + 9x_2 = 8x_2 + 9x_1$, which simplifies to $x_1 = x_2$, confirming the function is one-one.

To analyze surjectivity, let $y = f(x)$ and solve for $x$: $y(3x + 4) = 2x + 3$, so $3xy + 4y = 2x + 3$.

Rearranged, this becomes $x(3y - 2) = 3 - 4y$, giving $x = rac{3 - 4y}{3y - 2}$ when $3y - 2 eq 0$.

Hence, $y eq rac{2}{3}$, indicating the function is not onto if the codomain is $\mathbb{R}$, but is onto if the codomain is $\mathbb{R} \setminus \{ rac{2}{3}\}$.

The function is one-one, and onto if and only if the codomain excludes $ rac{2}{3}$, matching option C.

62244.subject: Mathematics
62244.text: If $\int \tan ^4 x \mathrm{dx}=a \tan ^3 x+\mathrm{b} \tan x+\mathrm{c} x+\mathrm{k}$ (where k is the constant of integration) then the value of $a-b+c=$
62244.sol:
Consider the integral I = $\int \tan^4 x dx$. Rewriting using the identity $\tan^2 x = \sec^2 x - 1$:

$I = \int \tan^2 x (\sec^2 x - 1) dx = \int \tan^2 x \sec^2 x dx - \int \tan^2 x dx$

For the first term, substitute $u = \tan x$, $du = \sec^2 x dx$:

$\int u^2 du = \frac{u^3}{3} = \frac{\tan^3 x}{3}$

For the second term, apply the identity again:

$\int \tan^2 x dx = \int (\sec^2 x - 1) dx = \tan x - x$

The complete integral becomes:

$I = \frac{\tan^3 x}{3} - \tan x + x + k$

Matching with the given form $a \tan^3 x + b \tan x + c x + k$ yields coefficients $a = \frac{1}{3}$, $b = -1$, $c = 1$. Therefore:

$a - b + c = \frac{1}{3} - (-1) + 1 = \frac{7}{3}$

66044.subject: Physics
66044.text: The potential difference that must be applied across the parallel and series combination of three identical capacitors such that the energy stored in them becomes the same. The ratio of potential difference in parallel to series combination is
66044.sol:
Let the capacitance of each identical capacitor be $C$.

For the parallel combination, the equivalent capacitance is $C_p = 3C$.

The energy stored in the parallel combination when a potential difference $V_p$ is applied is $U_p = \dfrac{1}{2}C_p V_p^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}(3C)V_p^2$.

For the series combination, the equivalent capacitance is $C_s = \dfrac{C}{3}$.

The energy stored in the series combination when a potential difference $V_s$ is applied is $U_s = \dfrac{1}{2}C_s V_s^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{C}{3}\right)V_s^2$.

Given that the energy stored in both combinations is the same, $U_p = U_s$.

$\dfrac{1}{2}(3C)V_p^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{C}{3}\right)V_s^2$

$3V_p^2 = \dfrac{V_s^2}{3}$

$\dfrac{V_p^2}{V_s^2} = \dfrac{1}{9}$

$\dfrac{V_p}{V_s} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

The ratio of potential difference in parallel to series combination is $1:3$.

Answer: $1:3$

Therefore, $\frac{E R}{(R+r)} \propto L$ In case of internal resistance measurement by potentiometer, considering two balance lengths $\left(L_1, L_2\right)$ corresponding to shunt resistors $\left(R_1, R_2\right)$ respectively, $\Rightarrow \frac{V_1}{V_2}=\frac{L_1}{L_2}=\frac{\left\{E R_1 /\left(R_1+r\right)\right\}}{\left\{E R_2 /\left(R_2+r\right)\right\}}=\frac{R_1\left(R_2+r\right)}{R_2\left(R_1+r\right)}$. Here, $L_1=1 \mathrm{~m}, L_2=1.5 \mathrm{~m}, ⇒ \frac{1}{1.5}=\frac{3(6+r)}{6(3+r)} 6+2r =9+1.5r $\Rightarrow r=6 \Omega

68654.text: A spring force constant $180$ N/m is loaded with a mass $0.2$ kg. The amplitude of oscillations is $4$ cm. When mass comes to equilibrium position, its velocity is
68654.sol:
Given $k = 180$ N/m, $m = 0.2$ kg, and $A = 4$ cm $= 0.04$ m.

The angular frequency of the spring-mass system is given by:

$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}}$

Substituting the given values:

$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{180}{0.2}} = \sqrt{900} = 30$ rad/s

The velocity of the mass at the equilibrium position is its maximum velocity, which is given by:

$v_\max = A\omega$

$v_\max = 0.04 \times 30 = 1.2$ m/s

Answer: $1.2$ m/s

70436.subject: Physics
70436.text: When the observer moves towards a stationary source with velocity '$V_1$', the apparent frequency of the emitted note is '$F_1$'. When the observer moves away from the source with velocity '$V_1$', the apparent frequency is '$F_2$'. If 'V' is the speed of sound in air and $F_1/F_2 = 2$, then $V/V_1 =$
70436.sol:
Using the Doppler effect formula, the apparent frequency when the observer moves towards the stationary source is given by

$F_1 = F_0 \left( \dfrac{V + V_1}{V} \right)

When$ the observer moves away from the stationary source, the apparent frequency is

F_2 = F_0 $\left( \dfrac{V - V_1}{V} \right)$

Given that $\dfrac{F_1}{F_2} = 2$, we can write

$\dfrac{V + V_1}{V - V_1} = 2$

$V + V_1 = 2V - 2V_1$

$3V_1 = V$

$\dfrac{V}{V_1} = 3$

Answer: $3$

70523.subject: Physics
70523.text: When source of sound moves towards a stationary observer, the apparent frequency heard by him
options: remains the same while wavelength decreases.
decreases and wavelength remains the same.
70523.sol:
For a sound source moving toward a stationary observer, the Doppler effect causes both frequency and wavelength to change.

The apparent frequency is given by $f' = f \left( \frac{v}{v - v_s} \right), where $ v$ is the speed of sound, $f$ is the source frequency, and $v_s$ is the source speed. Since $v_s > 0$, the denominator $v - v_s < v$, making $f' > f$. The frequency increases.

The apparent wavelength becomes \lambda' = \frac{v - v_s}{f}. Comparing to the original wavelength \lambda = \frac{v}{f}, we have \lambda' = \lambda - \frac{v_s}{f}, which is less than \lambda$ since $v_s > 0$. The wavelength decreases.

Therefore, both frequency increases and wavelength decrease, corresponding to option B.

71111.subject: Biology
71111.text:
Match List I with List II
List IList II
(A). Actual remains(I). Thin carbon film
(B). Moulds(II). They are hardened pieces of mineral matter.
(C). Cast(III). Plants, animals and human bodies got embedded in permafrost of artic or alpines snow.
(D). Compressions(IV). They are hardened encasement formed in the outer parts of organic matter.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
71111.sol:
Actual remains are the intact bodies or parts of organisms preserved without much alteration, such as plants, animals, and human bodies embedded in the permafrost of arctic or alpine snow.

Moulds are formed when an organism is buried in sediment and then decays, leaving a hollow cavity. They are hardened encasements formed in the outer parts of organic matter.

Casts are formed when minerals fill a mould and harden, creating a replica of the original organism. Thus, they are hardened pieces of mineral matter.

Compressions are fossils formed when organic matter is subjected to high pressure, leaving behind a thin carbon film.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A) - (III), (B) - (IV), (C) - (II), (D) - (I).

Answer: (A) - (III), (B) - (IV), (C) - (II), (D) - (I)

71173.subject: Biology
71173.text:
Select the correct sequence with respect to the process of spermatogenesis.
a) Primary spermatocyte
b) Primordial cell
c) Secondary spermatocyte
d) Spermatogonia
e) Spermatids
71173.sol:
Spermatogenesis is the process of formation of sperms in the seminiferous tubules of the testis.

The correct sequence of cells formed during spermatogenesis is:

Primordial germ cells (b) undergo mitotic divisions to produce Spermatogonia (d).

Some spermatogonia grow and increase in size to form Primary spermatocytes (a).

Primary spermatocytes undergo the first meiotic division (meiosis I) to form two haploid Secondary spermatocytes (c).

Secondary spermatocytes undergo the second meiotic division (meiosis II) to form four haploid Spermatids (e).

Spermatids eventually differentiate into spermatozoa (sperms).

Thus, the correct sequence is b \rightarrow d \rightarrow a \rightarrow c \rightarrow e.

Answer: b\rightarrow d\rightarrow a\rightarrow c\rightarrow e

71210.text: Which of the following forms hartig-net in the intercellular spaces of root cortex?
options: All biofertilizers which develope on roots
71210.sol:
Ectomycorrhizae form a dense sheath or mantle over the surface of the root. From this mantle, hyphae grow into the intercellular spaces of the root cortex, forming a highly branched network known as the Hartig net. This structure facilitates the exchange of nutrients between the fungus and the host plant.

Endomycorrhizae, on the other hand, penetrate the cell walls of the root cortex to form intracellular structures like arbuscules and vesicles, but they do not form a Hartig net.

Answer: Ectomycorrhizae

72337.subject: Physics
72337.text: In an oscillating LC circuit, the maximum charge on the capacitor is Q. When the energy is stored equally between the electric and magnetic fields, the charge on the capacitor is q. The relation between Q and q is
72337.sol:
Total energy of the LC circuit is given by the maximum energy stored in the capacitor:

$U_{total} = \dfrac{Q^2}{2C}$

When the energy is stored equally between the electric and magnetic fields, the electric energy $U_E$ is half of the total energy:

$U_E = \dfrac{1}{2} U_{total}$

The electric energy at this instant is given by:

$U_E = \dfrac{q^2}{2C}$

Equating the expressions for $U_E$:

$\dfrac{q^2}{2C} = \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \dfrac{Q^2}{2C} \right)

$ q^2 = $\dfrac{Q^2}{2}

$ Q = $\sqrt{2}$ q$

Answer: $Q = $\sqrt{2}$\, q

72421.subject: Physics
72421.text: Identify the INCORRECT statement for isobaric process.
72421.sol:
In an isobaric process, the pressure of the system remains constant, so $\Delta p = 0$.

The work done is given by $W = p\Delta V$. Since the volume changes, $W eq 0$.

The heat exchanged is $Q = nC_p\Delta T$. Since the temperature changes, $Q eq 0$.

The change in internal energy is $\Delta U = nC_v\Delta T$. Since the temperature changes, $\Delta U eq 0$.

The statement $\Delta U = 0$ is true for an isothermal process of an ideal gas, not an isobaric process. Therefore, $\Delta U = 0$ is the incorrect statement.

Answer: $\Delta U = 0$

72424.subject: Physics
72424.text: A gas for which $\gamma$ is $3/2$ is heated at constant pressure. The percentage of heat supplied for external work is nearly
72424.sol:
Heat supplied at constant pressure is given by $\Delta Q = n C_p \Delta T$

Work done by the gas is given by $\Delta W = P \Delta V = n R \Delta T$

The fraction of heat supplied used for external work is $\dfrac{\Delta W}{\Delta Q} = \dfrac{n R \Delta T}{n C_p \Delta T} = \dfrac{R}{C_p}$

Using Mayer's relation $C_p - C_v = R$ and $\gamma = \dfrac{C_p}{C_v}$, we get $C_p - \dfrac{C_p}{\gamma} = R$

$\dfrac{R}{C_p} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{\gamma}$

Given $\gamma = \dfrac{3}{2}$, substituting this value:

$\dfrac{\Delta W}{\Delta Q} = 1 - \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Percentage of heat used for external work $= \dfrac{1}{3} \times 100\% = 33.33\%$

This is nearly $33\%$.

Answer: $33\ \%$

72431.subject: Physics
72431.text: If R is the universal gas constant then the amount of heat needed to raise the temperature of 3 moles of an ideal monoatomic gas from 273 K to 393 K when no work is done is
72431.sol:
Since no work is done, the process is isochoric and the heat supplied is used entirely to increase the internal energy of the gas.

$Q = \Delta U = n C_v \Delta T$

For a monoatomic ideal gas, $C_v = \dfrac{3}{2} R$.

Given $n = 3$ moles, $T_1 = 273$ K, and $T_2 = 393$ K.

$\Delta T = 393 - 273 = 120$ K

Substituting the values:

$Q = 3 \times \dfrac{3}{2} R \times 120$

$Q = \dfrac{9}{2} R \times 120 = 540 R$

Answer: $540 \text{ R}$

75903.text: To a perpendicular to the plane of ecliptic, Earth's axis of rotation makes an angle of $23 \frac{1}{2}$ degrees. Had this angle been zero degree, which one among the following would result ?
options: There would have been no season
The length of day and night would have been the same throughout the year
The length of the day and night would have been the same all over the earth
75903.sol:
In astronomy, axial tilt (also called obliquity) is the
angle between an object's rotational axis and the
perpendicular to its Orbital plane, both oriented by the
right hand rule. At an obliquity of 0°, these lines point
in the same direction i.e. the rotational axis is
perpendicular to the orbital plane. Axial tilt differs from
inclination. Over the course of an orbit, the angle of
the axial tilt does not change, and the orientation of
the axis remains the same relative to the background
stars. This causes one pole to be directed toward the
Sun on one side of the orbit, and the other pole on the
other side, the cause of the seasons on the Earth.

82177.subject: Physics
82177.text: Power dissipated in an $L-C-R$ series circuit connected to an AC source of emf $\varepsilon$ is
82177.sol:
The emf of an LCR circuit is \(\varepsilon\).
The impedance of a series LCR circuit is given as,
\(Z=\sqrt{\left[R^2+\left(\omega L-\frac{1}{\omega C}\right)^2\right]}\)
The power factor in a series LCR circuit is given as,
\(\cos \phi=\frac{\mathrm{R}}{|\mathrm{Z}|}\)
The power dissipated in the circuit is given as,
\(\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{P}=\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{rms}} \mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{rms}} \cos \phi \\
& =\varepsilon \times \frac{\varepsilon}{|\mathrm{Z}|} \times \frac{\mathrm{R}}{|\mathrm{Z}|} \\
& =\frac{\varepsilon^2 \mathrm{R}}{\left[\mathrm{R}^2+\left(\omega \mathrm{L}-\frac{1}{\omega \mathrm{C}}\right)^2\right]}
\end{aligned}\)
Thus, the power dissipated in the series \(L C R\) circuit is \(\frac{\varepsilon^2 R}{\left[R^2+\left(\omega L-\frac{1}{\omega C}\right)^2\right]}\).

82700.text: In a region the potential is represented by $V\left(x, y, z\right) = 6x - 8xy - 8y + 6yz,$ where $V$ is in volts and $x, y, z,$ are in meters. The electric force experienced by a charge of $2$ coulombs situated at point $\left(1, 1, 1\right)$ is:
82700.sol:
Potential in the space varies as ${V}_{\left(x, y, z\right)} = 6x - 8xy - 8y + 6yz$.

Electric field is given by,
${E}_{x} = - \dfrac{∂ V}{∂ x} = - 6 + 8y$
${E}_{y} = - \dfrac{∂ V}{∂ y} = 8x + 8 - 6z$
${E}_{z} = - \dfrac{∂ V}{∂ z} = - 6y$
$\overset{\to}{E} = \left(- 6 + 8y\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(8x + 8 - 6z\right)\overset{^}{j} - 6y\overset{^}{k}$

Putting the value of the position we get,
${\overset{\to}{E}}_{\left(1, 1, 1\right)} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 10\overset{^}{j} - 6\overset{^}{k}$

Magnitude is given by,
$\left|\overset{\to}{E}\right| = 2\sqrt{35}N{C}^{- 1}$

Force on the charge is given by,
$F = qE = 2 \times 2\sqrt{35} = 4\sqrt{35}N$

85170.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: When many alleles of a single gene govern a character, it is called polygenic inheritance.
Statement II: In Polygenic inheritance, the effect of each allele is additive.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
85170.sol:
Polygenic inheritance refers to the inheritance of a trait governed by more than one gene.
In a polygenic trait the phenotype reflects the contribution of each allele i.e., the effect of each allele is additive.
Hence, statement I is incorrect and statement II is correct.

85293.subject: Zoology
85293.text: Which one of the following cannot be explained on the basis of Mendel's Law of Dominance?
options: The discrete unit controlling a particular character is called a factor
Out of one pair of factors one is dominant, and the other recessive
Alleles do not show any blending and both the characters recover as such in $\mathrm{F}_2$ generation
85293.sol:
The law of dominance does not occur universally. After Mendel several cases were recorded by scientists, where a clear deviation from law of dominance was seen. Such a deviation may be seen in the form of Incomplete dominance or Blending inheritance and Co-dominance.
Where $F_1$ hybrids exhibited a mixture or blending of character of two parents, the case is considered as that of incomplete dominance blending inheritance. It simply means that two genes of allelomorphic pair are not related as dominant or recessive, but each of them expresses itself partially. In the case of 4 o'clock plant, when plants with red flowers are crossed with plants having white flower, the $\mathrm{F}_1$ hybrids bear pink flower. When these pink flowers are self pollinated, they develop red, pink and white flowers in the ratio of $1: 2: 1$ respectively.

90798.text:
The function $f: R \to R$ is defined as $f\left(x\right) = {3}^{- x}$. From the following statements,

I. $f$ is one-one

II. $f$ is onto

III. $f$ is a decreasing function

the true statements are
90798.sol:
Since, $f: R \to R$ such that $f\left(x\right) = {3}^{- x}$

Let ${y}_{1}$ and ${y}_{2}$ be two elements of $f ( x )$ such that ${y}_{1} = {y}_{2}$

$⇒ {3}^{- {x}_{1}} = {3}^{- {x}_{2}} ⇒ {x}_{1} = {x}_{2}$

Since, if two images are equal, then their elements are equal, therefore it is one-one function.

Since, $f ( x )$ is positive for every value of $x$, therefore $f ( x )$ is into.

On differentiating w.r.t. $x$, we get $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = - {3}^{- x}log ⁡ 3 < 0$ for every value of $x$.

$∴$ It is decreasing function.

$∴$ Statement I and III are true.

Let equation of circle touching line $y = x + 2$ at $\left(2,4\right)$ is ${\left(x - 2\right)}^{2} + {\left(y - 4\right)}^{2} + \lambda\left(x - y + 2\right) = 0$ which passes through $\left(0,4\right)⇒ 4 + 0 + \lambda\left(0 - 4 + 2\right) ⇒ \lambda = 2$
$⇒$Equation of the required circle is $x^{2} + y^{2} - 2x - 10y + 24 = 0$
$⇒$~The radius of the circle is $\sqrt{{1}^{2} + {5}^{2} - 24} = \sqrt{2}$

91522.text: In a class tournament where the participants were to play one game with one another, two of the class players fell ill, having played $3$ games each. If the total number of games played is $27,$ then the number of participants at the beginning was

Since, these two players played $3$ matches each, hence the total number of matches is ${}^{n - 2}{C}_{2} + 3 + 3 = 27 ⇒ {}^{n - 2}{C}_{2} = 21$
${}^{n - 2}{C}_{2} = 21 ⇒ \dfrac{\left(n - 2\right)\left(n - 3\right)}{2} = \dfrac{7 \times 6}{2}$
$⇒ n - 2 = 7 ⇒ n = 9 .$

92962.text: If ${K}_{1}$ and ${K}_{2}$ are maximum kinetic energies of photoelectrons emitted when lights of wavelength ${\lambda}_{1}$ and ${\lambda}_{2}$ respectively incident on a metallic surface. If ${\lambda}_{1} = 3{\lambda}_{2},$ then
92962.sol:
Eienstein's photoelectric equation is given as,

${K}_{1} = hc \left(\dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{1}} - \dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{0}}\right) ...(i)

and ${K}_{2} = hc $\left(\dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{0}}\right)$ ...(ii)

Dividing Equation (i) by Equation (ii), we get

$\dfrac{{K}_{1}}{{K}_{2}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{1}} - \dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{0}}}{\dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{0}}}$

Since, ${\lambda}_{1} = 3{\lambda}_{2}$

$\dfrac{{K}_{1}}{{K}_{2}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{{3\lambda}_{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{0}}}{\dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{0}}}$

$= \dfrac{1}{{3\lambda}_{2}}\dfrac{\left(1 - \dfrac{3}{\left({\lambda}_{0} / {\lambda}_{2}\right)}\right)}{\dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{2}}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{0}}\right)}$

$\dfrac{{K}_{1}}{{K}_{2}} = \dfrac{1}{3}\dfrac{\left(1 - \dfrac{3}{\left({\lambda}_{0} / {\lambda}_{2}\right)}\right)}{\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{0} / {\lambda}_{2}}\right)}$

$\dfrac{{3K}_{1}}{{K}_{2}} = \dfrac{\left[1 - 3 / \left({\lambda}_{0} / {\lambda}_{2}\right)\right]}{\left(1 - 1 / \dfrac{{\lambda}_{0}}{{\lambda}_{2}}\right)} < 1$

$∴ \dfrac{{3K}_{1}}{{K}_{2}} < 1 ⇒ {K}_{1} < \dfrac{{K}_{2}}{3}$

Let electric flux linked with surfaces $A, BandC$ are${ϕ}_{A}, {ϕ}_{B}$and ${ϕ}_{C}$ respectively. That is

${ϕ}_{total} = {ϕ}_{A} + {ϕ}_{B} + {ϕ}_{C}$

Since ${ϕ}_{C} = {ϕ}_{A}$

$∴ 2{ϕ}_{A} + {ϕ}_{B} = {ϕ}_{total} = \dfrac{q}{{ε}_{0}}$

$or{ϕ}_{A} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{q}{{ε}_{0}} - {ϕ}_{B}\right)$

$But{ϕ}_{B} = ϕ\left(given\right)$

Hence,

${ϕ}_{A} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{q}{{ε}_{0}} - ϕ\right)$

93241.text: A satellite is revolving in a circular orbit at a height $h$ from the earth's surface, such that $h ≪ R$ where $R$& is the radius of the earth. Assuming that the effect of the earth's atmosphere can be neglected. What should be the minimum change required in the speed so that the satellite could escape from the gravitational field of earth?
93241.sol:
Orbital velocity ${v}_{0} = \sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{( R + h )}}$

Velocity required to escape the gravitational field, ${v}_{s} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{( R + h )}}$

Change in velocity $= \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{( R + h )}} - \sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{( R + h )}}$

If $h < < R$,
$\Deltav = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R}} - \sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{R}}$
$\Deltav = \sqrt{2gR} - \sqrt{gR}$

93281.subject: Physics
93281.text:
A projectile of mass $m$ is fired from the surface of the earth at an angle $\alpha = 6 {0}^{∘}$ from the vertical. The initial speed ${v}_{0}$ is equal to $\sqrt{\dfrac{{\text{GM}}_{\text{e}}}{{\text{R}}_{\text{e}}}}$. The maximum height that projectile can rise from the surface of the earth is $\dfrac{{\text{R}}_{\text{e}}}{\text{x}}$. Find the value of $x$?

$G$ = Universal Gravitational constant
${M}_{e}$ = Mass of earth
${R}_{e}$ = Radius of earth
93281.sol:
By conservation of angular momentum about C at position P and F

${\text{mv}}_{0} \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} {\text{R}}_{\text{e}} = \text{mv} {r}_{\text{max}}$

$⇒ \text{v} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3} {\text{R}}_{\text{e}} {\text{v}}_{0}}{2 {r}_{\text{max}}}$ ...(i)

By conservation of mechanical energy between P and F

$\dfrac{1}{2} {\text{mv}}_{0}^{2} - \dfrac{{\text{GM}}_{\text{e}} \text{m}}{{\text{R}}_{\text{e}}} = \dfrac{1}{2} {\text{mv}}^{2} - \dfrac{{\text{GM}}_{\text{e}} \text{m}}{{\text{r}}_{\text{max}}}$ ...(ii)

Put (i) in (ii)

$\dfrac{1}{2} {\text{mv}}_{0}^{2} - \dfrac{{\text{GM}}_{\text{e}} \text{m}}{{\text{R}}_{\text{e}}} = \dfrac{1}{2} \text{m} \dfrac{3 {\text{R}}^{2} {\text{v}}_{0}^{2}}{4 {r}_{\text{max}}^{2}} - \dfrac{{\text{GM}}_{\text{e}} \text{m}}{{\text{r}}_{\text{max}}}$

${\text{v}}_{0} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{\text{GM}}_{\text{e}}}{\text{R}}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2} \text{m} \dfrac{{\text{GM}}_{\text{e}}}{{\text{R}}_{\text{e}}} - \dfrac{{\text{GM}}_{\text{e}} \text{m}}{{\text{R}}_{\text{e}}} = \dfrac{3}{8} \dfrac{{\text{mR}}_{\text{e}}^{2}}{{\text{r}}_{\text{max}}^{2}} \dfrac{{\text{GM}}_{\text{e}}}{\text{R}} - \dfrac{{\text{GM}}_{\text{e}} \text{m}}{{\text{r}}_{\text{max}}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2 {\text{R}}_{\text{e}}} - \dfrac{1}{{\text{R}}_{\text{e}}} = \dfrac{3 \text{R}}{8 {r}_{\text{max}}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{\text{r}}_{\text{max}}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{- 1}{2 {\text{R}}_{\text{e}}} = \dfrac{3 {\text{R}}_{\text{e}} - 8 {r}_{\text{max}}}{8 {r}_{\text{max}}^{2}}$

$⇒ 4 {\text{r}}_{\text{max}}^{2} - 8 {\text{R}}_{\text{e}} {r}_{\text{max}} + 3 {\text{R}}_{\text{e}}^{2} = 0$

Solving the quadratic in rmax

we get

${\text{r}}_{\text{max}} = \dfrac{8 {\text{R}}_{\text{e}} \pm \sqrt{1 6} {\text{R}}_{\text{e}}}{8} = \dfrac{8 {\text{R}}_{\text{e}} \pm 4 {\text{R}}_{\text{e}}}{8}$

$⇒ {\text{r}}_{\text{max}} = \dfrac{8 {\text{R}}_{\text{e}} + 4 {\text{R}}_{\text{e}}}{8} = \dfrac{1 2 {\text{R}}_{\text{e}}}{8} = \dfrac{3 {\text{R}}_{\text{e}}}{2}$

$∴ {\text{h}}_{\text{max}} = {\text{r}}_{\text{max}} - {\text{R}}_{\text{e}} = \dfrac{3 {\text{R}}_{\text{e}}}{2} - {\text{R}}_{\text{e}} = \dfrac{{\text{R}}_{\text{e}}}{2}$

$∴ \text{x} = 2$

94470.text: A common emitter amplifier has a voltage gain of 50, an input impedance of 100 $Ω$ and an output impedance of 200 $Ω.$ The power gain of the amplifier is
94470.sol:
AC power gain = $\dfrac{Changeinoutputpower}{Changeininputpower}$

= $\dfrac{{∆ V}_{c} × {∆ i}_{c}}{{∆ V}_{i} × {∆ i}_{b}} = \left(\dfrac{{∆ V}_{c}}{{∆ V}_{i}}\right) × \left(\dfrac{{∆ i}_{c}}{{∆ i}_{b}}\right) = {A}_{V} × {β}_{AC}$

where ${A}_{V}isvoltagegain$ and ${\left(β\right)}_{AC}$ is AC current gain.

Also,

${A}_{V} = {β}_{AC} × resistancegain \left(= \dfrac{{R}_{o}}{{R}_{i}}\right)

Given, ${A}_{V} = 50, {R}_{o} = 200Ω, {R}_{i} = 100Ω$

Hence, 50 = ${β}_{AC} × $\dfrac{200}{100}

$∴{β}_{AC} = 25$

Now, AC power gain = ${A}_{V} × {β}_{AC}$ = 50 $×$ 25 = 1250$

95474.subject: Botany
95474.sol:
The presence or absence of coelom is an important basis of classifications in animals. Coelom refers to a large fluid-filled space lying between two outer body wall and inner digestive tube.

Schizocoelom arises from a mesodermal split. This body cavity is formed from blocks of mesoderm around the gut that enlarge and hollow out. Example- animals belonging to the Phyla Annelida, Mollusca and Arthropoda. Enterocoelom arises from out pocketing of the embryonic gut (endoderm). This type of body cavity is formed by out pocketing of the primitive gut that breaks off and forms the coelom. Example- animals belonging to the Phyla Echinodermata and Chordata.

96685.text: During ionic flux, uptake of ions into inner space is
96685.sol: The movement of ions is called flux. The movement of ions into the cell is called influx and outward migration of ions is known as efflux. The energy is considered to be involved in the transport of such free ions across the membrane. The absorption of ions, involving the use of metabolic energy, is called active absorption. Energy used in these mechanisms comes from metabolic activities. Mineral absorption is mainly an active process.

100498.subject: Physics
100498.text: Two particles of masses $m_1$ and $m_2$ are moving in concentric circles of radii $r_1$ and $r_2$ respectively. It is given that the ratio of their masses is $m_1 : m_2 = 1 : 2$ and the ratio of their radii is $r_1 : r_2 = 4 : 1$. If they have the same time period of revolution, the ratio of their centripetal forces $F_1 : F_2$ is:
100498.sol:
Time period $T$ is the same for both particles, so their angular velocity $\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T}$ is also the same.

The centripetal force is given by $F = m r \omega^2$.

The ratio of their centripetal forces is:
$\dfrac{F_1}{F_2} = \left(\dfrac{m_1}{m_2}\right) \left(\dfrac{r_1}{r_2}\right) \left(\dfrac{\omega_1}{\omega_2}\right)^2$

Substitute the given values:
$\dfrac{F_1}{F_2} = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) \times \left(\dfrac{4}{1}\right) \times (1)^2$

$\dfrac{F_1}{F_2} = \dfrac{2}{1}$

Thus, the ratio $F_1 : F_2$ is $2 : 1$.

Answer: $2 : 1$

101420.subject: Physics
101420.text: Two planets $A$ and $B$ have the same uniform mass density. The radius of planet $A$ is three times the radius of planet $B$. If $v_A$ and $v_B$ are the escape velocities on the surfaces of planets $A$ and $B$ respectively, then the ratio $\dfrac{v_A}{v_B}$ is :
101420.sol:
The escape velocity on the surface of a planet is given by $v = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R}}$.

Since the mass of a planet is $M = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3 \rho$, where $\rho$ is the uniform mass density, we can write:

$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{2G}{R} \left(\dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3 \rho\right)} = R\sqrt{\dfrac{8\pi G \rho}{3}}$

For planets with the same uniform density, the escape velocity is directly proportional to the radius ($v \propto R$).

Therefore, the ratio of their escape velocities is:

$\dfrac{v_A}{v_B} = \dfrac{R_A}{R_B}$

Given that $R_A = 3R_B$, we have:

$\dfrac{v_A}{v_B} = 3$

Answer: $3$

101666.subject: Physics
101666.text:
An open cylindrical vessel contains two immiscible liquids. A layer of water of height $2$ m is at the bottom, and a layer of oil of height $3$ m is on top. What is the absolute pressure at the bottom of the vessel?
(Given: density of water $= 1000$ kg m$^{-3}$, density of oil $= 800$ kg m$^{-3}$, atmospheric pressure $= 1.01 \times 10^5$ Pa, and $g = 10$ m/s$^2$)
101666.sol:
The absolute pressure at the bottom of the vessel is the sum of the atmospheric pressure and the pressure exerted by the two fluid columns.

Pressure due to the oil layer:
$P_{\text{oil}} = \rho_{\text{oil}} g h_{\text{oil}}$
$P_{\text{oil}} = 800 \times 10 \times 3 = 24,000$ Pa

Pressure due to the water layer:
$P_{\text{water}} = \rho_{\text{water}} g h_{\text{water}}$
$P_{\text{water}} = 1000 \times 10 \times 2 = 20,000$ Pa

Total gauge pressure at the bottom:
$P_{\text{gauge}} = P_{\text{oil}} + P_{\text{water}} = 24,000 + 20,000 = 44,000$ Pa $= 0.44 \times 10^5$ Pa

Absolute pressure at the bottom:
$P_{\text{abs}} = P_{\text{atm}} + P_{\text{gauge}}$
$P_{\text{abs}} = 1.01 \times 10^5 + 0.44 \times 10^5 = 1.45 \times 10^5$ Pa.

Answer: $1.45 \times 10^5$ Pa

107032.subject: Chemistry
107032.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
107032.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the properties of fluorine and chlorine:

Statement I: The negative electron gain enthalpy of $\text{Cl}$ is higher than that of $\text{F}$.
Statement II: The electronegativity of $\text{Cl}$ is higher than that of $\text{F}$.
Statement III: The bond dissociation enthalpy of $\text{Cl}_2$ is higher than that of $\text{F}_2$.
Statement IV: The first ionization enthalpy of $\text{F}$ is higher than that of $\text{Cl}$.

How many of the above statements are correct?
107032.sol:
Statement I is correct: The negative electron gain enthalpy of $\text{Cl}$ is higher than that of $\text{F}$ due to the small size of the $\text{F}$ atom, which leads to strong interelectronic repulsions in the compact $2p$ subshell.

Statement II is incorrect: Electronegativity strictly decreases down the group. $\text{F}$ is the most electronegative element in the periodic table, so its electronegativity is higher than that of $\text{Cl}$.

Statement III is correct: The bond dissociation enthalpy of $\text{F}_2$ is anomalously lower than that of $\text{Cl}_2$ because of the large electron-electron repulsions among the lone pairs in the small $\text{F}_2$ molecule.

Statement IV is correct: The first ionization enthalpy decreases down the group due to an increase in atomic size and shielding effect. Thus, $\text{F}$ has a higher ionization enthalpy than $\text{Cl}$.

Therefore, exactly three statements (I, III, and IV) are correct.

Answer: Only three

108675.subject: Chemistry
108675.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When an ideal gas undergoes adiabatic expansion, its internal energy decreases.

Reason (R): According to IUPAC sign convention, the work done by a system during expansion is taken as negative ($w < 0$).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
108675.sol:
Assertion (A) is true: In an adiabatic process, there is no heat exchange ($q = 0$). During expansion, work is done by the system, so $w < 0$. According to the first law of thermodynamics ($\Delta U = q + w$), $\Delta U = 0 + w$. Since $w$ is negative, $\Delta U$ is negative, meaning the internal energy decreases.

Reason (R) is true: By IUPAC convention in chemistry, work done by the system (expansion) is taken as negative.

However, Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation for Assertion (A). The decrease in internal energy is due to the combined effect of the process being adiabatic ($q = 0$) and the system doing work ($w < 0$). The mere sign convention for work does not explain the decrease in internal energy without specifying that $q = 0$. For instance, in an isothermal expansion, $w < 0$ but $\Delta U = 0$ because heat is absorbed ($q > 0$). Therefore, both statements are true, but the Reason is not the complete and correct explanation of the Assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion.

109358.subject: Chemistry
109358.text:
The solubility product ($K_{sp}$) values of four different silver salts at a certain temperature are given below:

Salt$K_{sp}$
$\text{AgCl}$$1.0 \times 10^{-10}$
$\text{Ag}_2\text{CrO}_4$$4.0 \times 10^{-12}$
$\text{Ag}_3\text{PO}_4$$2.7 \times 10^{-19}$
$\text{AgBr}$$1.0 \times 10^{-12}$


Which of the following salts has the highest molar solubility in water?
109358.sol:
To find the salt with the highest molar solubility, we calculate the molar solubility ($s$) for each salt from its $K_{sp}$.

1) For $\text{AgCl}$ (AB type):
$K_{sp} = s^2 \Rightarrow s = \sqrt{1.0 \times 10^{-10}} = 10^{-5}\text{ M}$

2) For $\text{Ag}_2\text{CrO}_4$ ($\text{A}_2\text{B}$ type):
$K_{sp} = 4s^3 \Rightarrow 4s^3 = 4.0 \times 10^{-12} \Rightarrow s^3 = 10^{-12} \Rightarrow s = 10^{-4}\text{ M}$

3) For $\text{Ag}_3\text{PO}_4$ ($\text{A}_3\text{B}$ type):
$K_{sp} = 27s^4 \Rightarrow 27s^4 = 2.7 \times 10^{-19} = 27 \times 10^{-20} \Rightarrow s^4 = 10^{-20} \Rightarrow s = 10^{-5}\text{ M}$

4) For $\text{AgBr}$ (AB type):
$K_{sp} = s^2 \Rightarrow s = \sqrt{1.0 \times 10^{-12}} = 10^{-6}\text{ M}$

Comparing the values, $\text{Ag}_2\text{CrO}_4$ has the highest molar solubility ($10^{-4}\text{ M}$). A common mistake is to simply look for the highest $K_{sp}$ value (which is $\text{AgCl}$), but the stoichiometry of the salt must be considered when relating $K_{sp}$ to solubility.

Answer: $\text{Ag}_2\text{CrO}_4$

111921.subject: Chemistry
111921.text: A mixture contains two isomers, $o$-nitrophenol and $p$-nitrophenol. Which of the following represents the most suitable technique for their separation and the correct underlying chemical reason?
options: Fractional distillation; due to a large difference in their molecular weights.
Distillation under reduced pressure; because both isomers decompose at their normal boiling points.
Steam distillation; because $o$-nitrophenol forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds with water making it highly soluble.
Steam distillation; because $o$-nitrophenol is steam volatile due to intramolecular hydrogen bonding while $p$-nitrophenol is not.
111921.sol:
The correct technique to separate a mixture of $o$-nitrophenol and $p$-nitrophenol is steam distillation.

$o$-Nitrophenol exhibits intramolecular hydrogen bonding, which prevents the association of its molecules, making it more volatile (steam volatile).

In contrast, $p$-nitrophenol exhibits intermolecular hydrogen bonding, leading to molecular association and a higher boiling point, making it less volatile.

Because of this significant difference in their steam volatility, steam distillation effectively separates the two isomers.

Answer: Steam distillation; because $o$-nitrophenol is steam volatile due to intramolecular hydrogen bonding while $p$-nitrophenol is not.

113911.subject: Chemistry
113911.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): For any aqueous solution with a density of exactly $1.0 \text{ g/mL}$, its molality is strictly greater than its molarity.
Reason (R): In such a solution, the mass of the solvent is strictly less than $1 \text{ kg}$ per Litre of the solution.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
113911.sol:
Let us consider $1 \text{ L}$ ($1000 \text{ mL}$) of an aqueous solution with a density of $1.0 \text{ g/mL}$.

Mass of the solution = Volume $\times$ Density = $1000 \text{ mL} \times 1.0 \text{ g/mL} = 1000 \text{ g}$.

We know that:
Mass of solution = Mass of solute + Mass of solvent
$\Rightarrow$ Mass of solvent = $1000 \text{ g} - \text{Mass of solute}$

Since the mass of the solute must be greater than zero for a solution to exist, the mass of the solvent will be strictly less than $1000 \text{ g}$ (or $< 1 \text{ kg}$). Thus, Reason (R) is correct.

Now, let the number of moles of solute in this $1 \text{ L}$ solution be $n$.
Molarity ($M$) = $\dfrac{n}{1 \text{ L}} = n$

Molality ($m$) = $\dfrac{\text{Moles of solute}}{\text{Mass of solvent (in kg)}}$
Since the mass of the solvent is less than $1 \text{ kg}$, the denominator is a fraction less than $1$.
Therefore, Molality = $\dfrac{n}{<1} > n$

Hence, Molality > Molarity. Assertion (A) is correct.

Reason (R) correctly explains why the denominator in the molality formula is less than $1$, which mathematically causes the molality to exceed the molarity. Therefore, both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

Later when the linkages were established, the fungi were correctly identified and moved out of deuteromycetes. Once perfect (sexual) stages of members of dueteromycetes were discovered they were often moved to ascomycetesand basidiomycetes. The deuteromycetes reproduce only by asexual spores known as conidia. 121379.text: What type of genetic material do viruses that infect animals have?

A virus is a nucleoprotein and the genetic material is infectious. In general, viruses that infect plants have single stranded RNA and <mark style="background-color: yellow, turquious;"> viruses that infect animals have either single or double stranded RNA or double stranded DNA. </mark>Bacterial viruses or bacteriophages (viruses that infect the bacteria) are usually double stranded DNA viruses. The protein coat called capsid made of small subunits called capsomeres, protects the nucleic acid. These capsomeres are arranged in helical or polyhedralgeometric forms. Viruses cause diseases like mumps, small pox, herpes and influenza. AIDS in humans is also caused by a virus. In plants, the symptoms can be mosaic formation, leaf rolling and curling, yellowing and vein clearing, dwarfing and stunted growth.

121589.text:

Assertion (A) is not correct but Reason (R) is correct.
121589.sol:
Assertion (A) is correct because Mycoplasma are indeed the smallest living cells known.

Reason (R) is also correct as Mycoplasma completely lack a cell wall and can survive without oxygen.

However, the lack of a cell wall and the ability to survive without oxygen do not explain why they are the smallest living cells. These are independent factual characteristics of Mycoplasma.

Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

121623.text: Among rust, smut and mushroom all the three
121623.sol: Rust, smut and mushroom all belong to the group of pathogenic fungi. These fungi belong to the class basidiomycetes, and produce basidiospores. Mushroom are placed in the order agaricales. Amanita and Marasmius are pathogenic or disease causing fungi. Marasmius ordeades causes fairy rings on turf grasses. Rusts and smuts are included in the subclass teliomycetidae. Rust fungi comes under order uredinales, eg. Puccinia graminis causes black rust of wheat, $P$. recondita causes leaf rust of wheat.
